A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same self-attention CNN study of macaque V1 responses. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional appendix analyses in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original neural-response prediction experiments on M1S1 and M2S1, including model comparisons, incremental-learning experiments, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds receptive-field measurements, simulated surround-suppression tests, and comparisons with a recurrent CNN.

M1.justification: The proposed CNN architectures, self-attention components, readout variants, MSE objective, and incremental-learning procedures remain unchanged in Sections 3.1–3.4. The newly evaluated recurrent CNN is a comparator.

E1.justification: The macaque datasets and natural-image prediction task remain unchanged. Appendix A.13 adds a distinct test scenario using center-only and annular surround gratings of varying diameters to probe contextual suppression, extending the earlier stimulus-preference analyses.

E2.justification: Figure 16 adds a recurrent CNN with one layer and seven iterations to direct M2S1 comparisons against ff-CNN and ff+sa-CNN. v2 cited recurrent-network research but did not report this comparison. The existing shared-core factorized and VGG transfer-learning comparisons in Figure 8 are retained.

E3.justification: The original training and evaluation settings remain unchanged. Added supplemental protocols include Gaussian-fitted receptive-field mapping for 279 neurons, grating-diameter sweeps with a 95%-response criterion for the grating summation field, and M2S1 comparisons at 12.5%, 25%, and 100% training data.

E4.justification: Appendices A.12–A.14 substantially extend supplementary validation: receptive-field maps and a population distribution test spatial plausibility, center/surround stimulation tests physiological suppression, and recurrent-model comparisons examine relative data efficiency. These address additional validation questions beyond the retained architectural ablations and attention visualizations.

E5.justification: The SEM reporting in Tables 1–3 and Figure 5 is retained. v3 introduces no training-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or specified inferential tests; Figure 16 supplies additional scores without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their values, while Figures 14–16 add substantial physiological and comparative results. Figure 16 reports ff+sa-CNN versus recurrent-CNN correlations of 0.498 versus 0.435 at full data and 0.272 versus 0.291 at 12.5%. At 25%, self-attention has higher correlation, 0.317 versus 0.298, while recurrence has higher peak-tuning scores. These are newly reported comparisons, not demonstrated gains over v2.

T1.justification: The peak-tuning definition and existing mathematical content are unchanged. The additions describe empirical receptive-field and stimulation protocols, without introducing new theoretical assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the central claims about self-attention improving prediction, complementary contextual mechanisms, and the benefits of incremental learning. Changing 'feature preference' to 'top feature preference' clarifies wording without altering the contribution.

C2.justification: The new appendices interpret receptive-field sizes and suppression responses as consistent with physiological observations and qualify comparative performance as data-dependent. However, A.14 overgeneralizes recurrent-model superiority at 25% or less: Figure 16 supports superior peak tuning at 25%, but not superior correlation.

D1.justification: The code-access disclosure moves from A.12 to A.15 and replaces the anonymous repository address with a named GitHub repository. v3 also specifies the new recurrent comparator's one-layer, seven-iteration configuration and describes the added stimulation procedures. Existing implementation and training details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Pan et al. (2023) on contextual suppression in CNNs and Cavanaugh et al. (2002) as the physiological reference for the new replication. It also relates the recurrent-model data-efficiency findings to the already cited Zhang et al. (2022). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization remain intact. v3 adds ethics and acknowledgments sections, updates author affiliations and correspondence information, makes small heading and caption edits, and inserts three appendix sections before the relocated code disclosure.

P2.justification: Figures 14–16 add receptive-field maps and a histogram, physiological response plots, and three comparison tables presented as figure panels. Figure 1 is rearranged and resized, Figure 3 becomes a smaller display beside wrapped text, and Figure 5 is enlarged. Existing scientific content in Figures 2–13 is retained.

improvement.justification: The added physiological checks and recurrent-model comparison provide useful validation and context missing from v2. The gain is limited by reporting problems: A.14 claims recurrent superiority at 25% data despite Figure 16 showing higher self-attention correlation, 0.317 versus 0.298. Overall, the additions strengthen the evidence modestly while leaving the core method and findings unchanged.
